start.text: The chapter will sit. I've said so, and I'll say it again until the candles let it.
Still choosing for yourself, Wakebearer? I've not stopped hoping you'll tire of it.
Wakebearer. Have you thought on the rite?

first.text: A tall woman in a white robe stands at the top of the chapter-house steps, a red stole over her shoulders and her hands folded at her waist, as if she has stood exactly there since the bell.
Wakebearer. Forgive me not coming down to the quay. Nobody on Kindleby goes further from the candles than they must. Not even me.
Agathe Lorn. Provost of Kindleby. These days that means I'm the most senior Keeper anyone can find.
Have we met? ...No. I'd remember an ember.
Four lights. The Gull, the Ridge, the Heron, the Wrack. We've had the news of every one off the Tidewright decks, a week late and wrong in the particulars. You'll tell me the particulars, one day.
You carry a sleeve-ember. That's off a Spire robe, and it's been picked off with a thumbnail. ...Aldous Wren. He always did pick at things.
He ran home to Saltmarrow, then. They all ran, that night. Aldous ran the furthest, and the least far.
There's a story going round the Tidewright decks that Keepers put the Spire out. On purpose. It started on Wrackholm, they say, from a stranger with an ember.
I'd like it to stop. Stories like that get people drowned.
And sworn a friend of the lanes, I hear. Their oath is about decks. Ours is about light. A person can carry both, if they're careful which one they set down first.

choice.text: What would it take to light the Vigil Light?
Aldous told me the High Keeper put the flame out.
Wynn Sallow is alive. He keeps the Ridge Light on Thornwold.
There's a Keeper at the Ridge Light on Thornwold. He calls himself the Lamp.
There are colliers on the Northing's boat-stage, waiting for the Spire's boat. I promised I'd tell the Spire.

rite.text: Her hand goes to the long iron key on the chain at her belt, and rests there.
The Vigil Light, on the crown of the island above us. Dark, like the rest were. I have the key.
It will be lit, Wakebearer, and you will light it, and I thank the flame for you every night. But not the way the others were.
On four islands now you chose what was burned. You. Alone. A stranger with an ember, at the top of a stair, with whoever happened to be standing near.

That was never how it was done. For nine hundred years a Keeper chose. The chapter sat, and weighed, and chose what an island could spare, and the island never had to. That's what a Keeper is: one who chooses, so that others needn't.
So I'll ask you plainly. Bow to the rite. Let the chapter sit and choose Kindleby's burning, and carry its choice up the stair. That's all.

choice.text: I'll choose, as I've chosen everywhere.
And if the chapter chooses wrong?

wrong.text: Then it will be the chapter's wrong, and not yours. Is that so small a thing to be given?

bowed.text: For a moment she looks very much older, and then she doesn't.
You don't know what it is to us, to have the thing done properly. Once. Since.
The chapter will sit. Not tonight; there are brothers and sisters on the candles, and the candles come first. But it will sit.

refused.text: Then the chapter will sit anyway, and choose anyway, and you'll do as you please at the top of the stair.
We'll see which of us Kindleby thanks. I don't think it'll be either.

aldous.text: Aldous Wren was a door-warden on the east stair, and he was drinking before he was a novice. He told you the High Keeper put out the Firstflame.
The order's word is that the Firstflame failed. The High Keeper was at the flame when it failed, and has not been seen since. That is what the order knows.
He saw a light go down the stair past him, that night.
She is quiet long enough for a candle on the sill behind her to gutter and recover.
If Aldous Wren has seen something, he can come to Kindleby and say it to the chapter. I'd send a boat for him. Tell him so.

lamp_told.text: She says it like a word in a language she used to speak.
Every beacon-keeper who'd sent no word by spring we wrote into the Long Book among the lost. Wynn Sallow of the Ridge Light among them. Thirty years on that ridge, and I wrote him off in a line.
I'll have the line struck through. We don't scrape a name out of the Long Book. We strike it, so anybody can see it was once wrong.

lamp_left.text: The Lamp. That's not a name, Wakebearer, that's a post. Every beacon-keeper is the Lamp to somebody.
The Ridge Light's keeper is in the Long Book. If he's chosen to go by no name, he'll have had his reasons. It's his to choose.

stage.text: The Northing's stage. Keepers' boats put in there once a month with oil and meal, for longer than anybody's counted.
And they've waited on it three months. For a boat from the Spire.
There is no Spire to tell, Wakebearer. There's me.
Very well. You've told the Spire. When the chapter sits I'll put it to them that the skiff goes north, with oil and meal and a lantern, and brings back whoever wants bringing.

quiet.text: Those the fog had. Brothers and sisters off the Spire who came over in the boats Hushed, and anybody the boats have found drifting since.
We keep them warm, and fed, and near the candles. It's the oldest work of the order, Wakebearer. Older than the beacons. To keep the Hushed.
You can't go in. Not with that in your hand. They've had enough of other people's light.
